name: Kaiserklamm
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaiserklamm Gorge near Brandenberg is a wild ravine carved by the Brandenberger Ache, featuring cliff-hewn trails, rushing whitewaters, and timber-drifting heritage.
preis: Gorge path freely accessible (voluntary conservation contribution requested); parking fee at Kaiserhaus
oeffnungszeiten: Open May through October in dry weather; strictly closed during heavy rainfall and winter
beschreibung:
Überblick

The awe-inspiring Kaiserklamm Gorge is celebrated as one of the wildest and most evocative natural defiles in the Austrian Alps. Carved deeply into the forested limestone topography of the Brandenberg Alps, this protected natural monument lies approximately ten kilometres north of the sunny mountain village of Brandenberg. Here, the torrential Brandenberger Ache river surges through sheer vertical cliffs, subterranean rock kettles, and frothing eddies with raw geological power. Named in honour of Austrian Emperor Franz Joseph I, who marveled at its pristine rapids during an imperial hunting trip, the canyon holds deep cultural importance. For centuries, daring loggers utilized these tempestuous waters for timber drifting ('Holztrift'), driving vast tree trunks down into the Inn Valley. Today, a masterful rock-cut footpath fitted with steel cable handrails hugs the vertical chasm, affording walkers spellbinding close-up views into turquoise torrents.

Route & Anforderungen

The journey through Kaiserklamm commences directly at the historic Kaiserhaus inn and follows the riverbed upstream. The secured gorge path spans approximately one kilometre, requiring 30 to 45 minutes of walking time in each direction with negligible elevation variance. Narrow cantilevered timber boardwalks, hollowed rock galleries, and observation decks present dramatic perspectives into whirlpools and polished limestone flutes. At the canyon's upper terminus, hikers can retrace their footsteps or return via an easy, wide forest access road to complete a scenic loop. Supportive hiking shoes with deep rubber tread are mandatory, as mist keeps rock slabs slick. Young children should be tethered to safety cables via safety harnesses; the narrow gorge walkway is entirely inaccessible for prams and wheelchairs.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists arrive via motorway A12 (exit Kramsach) and continue on regional road L4 through Brandenberg to the Aschau hamlet and Gasthof Kaiserhaus, where paid parking is available. Regional buses run from Kramsach and Brixlegg train stations into Brandenberg, with designated seasonal shuttles serving Kaiserhaus.

Tipps

Do not miss sampling the authentic Brandenberger Prügeltorte at the historic Gasthof Kaiserhaus. Baked slowly on an open beechwood spit over flickering flames, this layered cake specialty is an iconic culinary heirloom of the Brandenberg Valley.
